tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, do NOT push, do NOT touch .git. You own exactly three paths and must create or edit nothing else: bench/affordance_map.py, tests/test_affordance_map.py, bench/affordance_known_gaps.json. Do not edit any story package file under data/ or tests/fixtures/ (they are ground truth; gaps you find are reported, never fixed).

GOAL: build "L0" of the scene-affordance E2E plan (.plans/scene-affordance-e2e.md section 4 L0, read that section and sections 2-3 first). L0 is a free, deterministic bench tool that derives, from a story package alone, which things, places and people the player must act on for each scene transition ("affordances"), then static checks over that map. It is a test tool in bench/, never runtime code, and must be story-agnostic: no scene ids, entity ids or story words hard-coded. It must work on both data/stories/continuity-initiative and tests/fixtures/stories/lighthouse-keeper (the fixture has no earn_when knowledge, so it has few or no player-earned affordances; the tool must handle that without error and its checks must still pass there).

READ FIRST (read-only): AGENTS.md; storygame/story_package/models.py (Transition, FactPredicate, KnowledgeDefinition with earn_when/action_evidence/entity_ids/requires/establishes/must_convey/delivery_text, FactDelivery, StoryletRoute, CanonicalRouteEvent, PacingEvent/PacingRealization, SceneMetadata with entry_text/item_placements/character_placements/item_ids/participant_ids/bridge_text, SceneBeat.details, Entity name/aliases, Item.hidden, WorldEffect.reveal, SceneFrame); storygame/story_package/loader.py (load_story_package(Path), and the existing validators _validate_transition_trigger_sources and _validate_required_reveal_prerequisites, which already do part of this; do not duplicate their error logic, but your findings are reported, not raised). Look at bench/jev_use.py for bench module style. Match surrounding code style.

BUILD bench/affordance_map.py with:
1. build_affordance_map(package) -> dict (JSON-serialisable) with {"story_id", "scenes": [{"scene_id", "transitions": [...], "gates": [...]}]} covering every scene in package.scenes in order. Each transition entry: id, target_scene_id, triggers (fact_id, equals), required_dependencies. Each GATE is one transition trigger fact (equals true) with: transition_id, fact_id, and "sources": every producer of that fact in the transition's source scene:
   - kind "knowledge": a knowledge item whose available_in_scenes includes the scene and whose establishes asserts the fact (or whose establishes asserts it via a fact the item lists);
   - kind "handoff": a FactDelivery (package.deliveries) with that fact_id, or whose costs assert it;
   - kind "storylet": a storylet route realization operation, or a bridge/resolution event operation, asserting it in that scene;
   - kind "engine": a pacing event in that scene whose effects set it true; carry its at_turn, its `when` conditions and its realization texts.
   Each source records id, kind, player_earned (true for knowledge with earn_when, or a storylet/bridge route that needs a player action; false for engine and unconditional events), earn_when, the earliest turn window if the package gives one, and "requires" (fact predicates) resolved recursively, with a visited-set so cycles cannot loop.
   For player-earned sources, "affordances" = the world entities the player must act on: the source's entity_ids, plus every non-verb group of action_evidence (the first group is the verbs; each later group is a set of alternative words; resolve each group to world entities by matching entity name or alias, case-insensitive, whole-word; keep unresolved groups in an "unresolved_terms" list rather than dropping them), plus the affordances of every source that produces a fact in its `requires` chain. Each affordance: entity_id, name, kind (item/location/npc/group), gate it belongs to, source id, "visible_at_entry" (true when the entity is the scene's location, a participant, or placed in the scene by item_placements/character_placements/item_ids and not hidden), and "revealed_by" (id of the earlier source in the same gate that reveals it, when it is not visible at entry: e.g. a hidden item in the requires chain, or an entity named in an earlier source's entity_ids).
   Also include per scene: "entry_material": the list of player-facing text strings the narrator gets for that scene, with a label for each: SceneMetadata.entry_text, scene frame situation, opening beat prose and details, every beat's details, item_placements text, character_placements text, bridge_text going in. Engine-source realization texts are listed under their gate.
2. check_affordance_map(package, amap) -> list of Finding dicts {"check": 1|2|3|4, "scene_id", "gate" (transition_id:fact_id), "subject", "message"} implementing exactly these four checks from the plan: (1) every transition has at least one gate whose sources are non-empty and whose `requires` facts all resolve to some source in the same scene or to a fact the scene entry guarantees (the scene_<id>_entry_known convention used in loader.py, or a bridge-event guarantee from the previous scene; read how _validate_required_reveal_prerequisites decides this and mirror it); report a trigger fact with no source and a dangling requires; (2) every affordance of a player-earned source resolves to a world entity that is visible_at_entry or has a revealed_by; (3) every affordance's name or any alias appears (case-insensitive, whole word) in that scene's entry_material, or in must_convey/delivery_text/fallback_text of an earlier source in the same gate (that is the prompt-side half: the narrator could show it); (4) every engine source has at least one realization text. Equals-false triggers are listed in the map but produce no gate.
3. A CLI: `uv run python -m bench.affordance_map --package <dir> [--out <file>] [--findings]` loads the package with load_story_package, writes the map JSON (to --out or stdout, with "findings" included as a top-level list) and prints a one-line summary per scene to stderr. Exit 0 always for the map; with --strict exit 1 when there are findings.
Keep functions small and typed, ruff-clean (line length per pyproject), no new dependencies, no network, no model calls.

BUILD tests/test_affordance_map.py (hermetic, no live worker; follow other tests/ files for how they load packages):
- Small unit tests on a tiny synthetic package, built by loading the lighthouse-keeper fixture and/or constructing with model_copy(update=...) variants: a gate with an engine source, a player-earned knowledge source with an action_evidence object group resolving to a visible entity, a hidden entity that is revealed_by an earlier source, and one negative case per check (1-4) proving a deliberately broken variant produces a Finding with the right check number. Also a cycle in `requires` terminates.
- Whole-package tests for both packages: every scene in the chain has an entry; the map is JSON-serialisable; checks 1, 2 and 4 return no findings; and check-3 findings (plus any others) for the shipped continuity-initiative package equal EXACTLY the recorded list in bench/affordance_known_gaps.json (a list of {check, scene_id, gate, subject}). Extra findings fail (new gap); missing findings fail too (stale entry), with a message saying which to add or remove. The lighthouse-keeper package must have no findings.
- If checks 1, 2 or 4 do find real gaps in the shipped package, do NOT fix the package: put them in the known-gaps file too and make the test compare ALL checks against that file, and say so in notes.md.
Generate bench/affordance_known_gaps.json by running the tool on the shipped package (sorted by scene_id, gate, subject, check; indent 2, trailing newline).

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root, absolute tools available): 
  TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q -n0 tests/test_affordance_map.py
  TMPDIR=/tmp uv run python -m bench.affordance_map --package data/stories/continuity-initiative --out /tmp/cm.json
  TMPDIR=/tmp uv run ruff check --fix bench/affordance_map.py tests/test_affordance_map.py && TMPDIR=/tmp uv run ruff format bench/affordance_map.py tests/test_affordance_map.py
Never call a live model or the network. The check will fail unless: only your three files changed, tests pass, ruff is clean, both packages map without error, the continuity-initiative map has all nine scenes, and its 1A gates include michelle_drawer and memory_card as affordances (the KMS drawer and the memory card behind it are the motivating example; if your map does not reach them, fix the derivation, not the check).

OUTPUT CONTRACT: also write ./notes.md at the worktree root (it is excluded from the diff by the check; do not add it to git) listing: the files you read, the derivation rules you chose where this brief left judgment, the number of findings per check on each package, and any assumption.
tasks.verified: only the three owned files changed; the new tests, ruff, the CLI on both packages and the 1A drawer/memory-card assertion pass; the patch is exported to ringer-work/affordance-l0/l0.patch
